fullPassage: Now that day seems like a dream to me. I remember the two old men sitting at the table and the soft sounds of the Maori words as they talked. All through the quiet afternoon and into the evening, they recalled missing names. I had a strange feeling that there were other people in the room. I felt as if people from the past were looking over the shoulders of the two old men to see if the work was correct. Finally, they stopped. It was done. After a moment of silence, the old man whispered to Nani, “Goodbye, friend.” Crying, they pressed their noses together to say goodbye.

questions.passage: For some time, my grandfather had been busy writing down the village genealogy, known as the whakapapa. ① The whakapapa had been in his old house. But then came the night of the fire, which ran through the house and destroyed our past. ② Trying to find a way out of the ashes of the past, Nani began to write the whakapapa again with his shaky hands. ③ He chanted the names of the ancestors, joining the past to the present once more. ④
questions.stem:
다음 글에서 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?

"In only one night, everything we knew was gone. Nani Tama, in despair, went to stay with his daughter, my Auntie Hiraina."

det.korean: 화재로 집이 파괴된 직후, 하룻밤에 모든 것을 잃고 절망에 빠져 딸 집에 머물게 되었다는 내용이 와야 한다. 그 다음에 "잿더미에서 길을 찾으며" 다시 쓰기 시작하는 내용으로 이어진다.
det.analysis:
✅ ②: 화재 묘사 직후 → 결과(모든 것 상실 + 절망) → 재작성 시작으로 자연스러운 흐름
❌ ①: 아직 화재 언급 전
❌ ③: 이미 재작성 시작 → 시간 순서 역전
❌ ④: 낭송 시작 후 → 문맥 불일치
det.tip: 시간 순서: 화재 → 상실/절망 → 재작성 시도

questions.passage: We traveled all night, mostly in silence, listening to Nani chanting in the darkness. ① It was strange but wonderful to hear him. ② Sometimes, he burst into a song that he had taught Auntie. ③ Just before noon, we arrived at a small town called Murupara. ④
questions.stem:
다음 글에서 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?

"They sang together, lifting up their voices to send the song flying like a bird through the sky."

det.korean: 할아버지가 고모에게 가르쳐준 노래를 부르기 시작한 후, 그들이 함께 노래하는 장면이 와야 한다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③: "burst into a song that he had taught Auntie" 직후 → "They sang together"로 자연스러운 연결
❌ ①: 아직 노래 언급 전
❌ ②: 낭송 감상 중 → 노래와 직접 연결 안 됨
❌ ④: 도착 후 → 여행 중 장면이 아님
det.tip: "burst into a song" → "They sang together": 노래 시작 → 함께 부르는 장면

questions.passage: It was early morning and still dark when we returned to Auntie’s place. All the lights were on, and the village people were waiting for us. Smiling, Nani Tama lifted up the whakapapa and offered it to the village. Our hearts were full because __________________________________________.
questions.stem:
다음 주어진 단어를 올바른 순서로 배열하시오.

grandfather / had / for / saved / our / past / us / our

det.korean: "our grandfather had saved our past for us" → 할아버지가 우리를 위해 과거를 구해 냈다.
det.analysis:
our grandfather(주어) + had saved(과거완료 동사) + our past(목적어) + for us(전치사구)
과거완료 had saved: 귀환 시점(과거)보다 앞선 동작
det.tip: 주어(our grandfather) + had p.p.(had saved) + 목적어(our past) + 전치사구(for us)

questions.wa: our grandfather had saved our past for us
accept: our grandfather had saved our past for us
Our grandfather had saved our past for us

questions.passage: For some time, my grandfather had been busy ①<u>writing</u> down the village genealogy, ②<u>known</u> as the whakapapa. The whakapapa had been in his old house. But then came the night of the fire, ③<u>which</u> ran through the house and ④<u>destroyed</u> our past. In only one night, everything we knew ⑤<u>were</u> gone.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~⑤ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ⑤ were → was: 주어 everything은 단수 취급이므로 단수 동사 was가 적절하다.
det.analysis:
❌ ⑤ were: everything은 단수 → was
✅ ① writing: be busy ~ing → 올바름
✅ ② known: 과거분사 → "~로 알려진"
✅ ③ which: 관계대명사 (선행사 the fire)
✅ ④ destroyed: 과거형 동사 (ran과 병렬)
det.tip: everything/everyone/nobody 등 = 단수 취급 → 단수 동사(was/is/has)

questions.passage: Trying to find a way out of the ashes of the past, Nani began to write the whakapapa again with his shaky hands. He chanted the names of the ancestors, __________ the past to the present once more.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 주절(chanted)과 동시에 일어나는 동작 → 분사구문 joining
det.analysis:
✅ ③ joining: 동시동작 분사구문
❌ ① join: 원형 불가
❌ ② joined: 접속사 없이 두 동사 연결 불가
❌ ④ to be joined: 수동 부정사 → 부적절
det.tip: 주절, ~ing: 동시에 일어나는 동작을 나타내는 분사구문

questions.passage: I had a strange feeling that there were other people in the room. I felt __________ people from the past were looking over the shoulders of the two old men to see if the work was correct.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: "마치 과거의 사람들이 보고 있는 것처럼 느꼈다" → as if(마치 ~인 것처럼)
det.analysis:
✅ ① as if: 가정/비유 → "마치 ~인 것처럼"
❌ ② even if: 양보 → "~하더라도"
❌ ③ so that: 목적 → "~하기 위해"
❌ ④ in case: 대비 → "~할 경우를 대비해"
det.tip: feel as if + 가정법: 마치 ~인 것처럼 느끼다

questions.passage: Sometimes, there were lines that were difficult to ①<u>remember</u>. Then his voice suddenly ②<u>stopped</u> in the middle of the chant. The village waited in worried ③<u>excitement</u> until the next name burst out of his mouth. It took Nani Tama almost two years to ④<u>gather</u> most of the whakapapa, but there were still ⑤<u>missing</u> names he needed to fill in.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~⑤ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: 원문은 "worried silence"(걱정 어린 침묵). ③ excitement(흥분)은 silence의 반의어로 부적절.
det.analysis:
❌ ③ excitement(흥분): 원문 silence(침묵) → 걱정스럽게 기다리는 상황에 흥분은 부적절
✅ ① remember(기억하다): 원문 일치
✅ ② stopped(멈췄다): 원문 일치
✅ ④ gather(모으다): 원문 일치
✅ ⑤ missing(빠진): 원문 일치
det.tip: silence(침묵) ↔ excitement(흥분) — "waited in worried ___": 걱정 어린 침묵이 자연스러움

questions.passage: When I arrived at Auntie’s place, I was shocked to see how thin Nani Tama was. “Look, Nani,” I said. “I’m not taking you anywhere. You could die on me!” Nani looked at me in __________.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 손주가 데려가지 않겠다고 하자 할아버지는 화가 나서(anger) 쳐다보았다. 바로 뒤에 "너는 내가 이 방에서 죽기를 바라느냐?"라고 반박한다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ anger(분노): 손주의 거부에 대한 반응 → 뒤 대사의 강한 어조와 일치
❌ ① joy: 거부당한 상황에 부적절
❌ ② curiosity: 문맥과 무관
❌ ③ confusion: 뒤 대사가 명확한 항의 → 혼란이 아님
det.tip: "looked at me in anger" → 뒤따르는 대사의 강한 어조("You want me to die here?")가 단서

questions.passage: Now that day seems like a __________ to me. I remember the two old men sitting at the table and the soft sounds of the Maori words as they talked.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 그날은 마치 꿈(dream)처럼 느껴진다. 비현실적이면서도 아름다운 기억.
det.analysis:
✅ ② dream: "seems like a dream" → 비현실적이지만 경이로운 경험
❌ ① happiness: "seems like happiness"는 부자연스러움
❌ ③ nightmare: 부정적 → 긍정적 기억과 불일치
❌ ④ reality: "seems like reality"는 모순 (이미 현실)
det.tip: seems like a dream = 꿈같다 — 비현실적이면서도 아름다운 경험을 표현

questions.passage: The old man held on tightly to the side of the bed and cried out as he stood up. Every slow, __________ (pain) step hurt him, but he tried to walk.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 어법에 맞게 변형하여 쓰시오.

det.korean: pain(명사) → painful(형용사): 명사 step을 수식하는 형용사 필요. "고통스러운 걸음"
det.analysis:
pain(명사) → painful(형용사)
빈칸 뒤 step(명사)을 수식하는 형용사 필요
painful step = 고통스러운 걸음
det.tip: pain → painful / hope → hopeful / care → careful — 명사 → -ful 형용사화

questions.passage: __________ (tradition), the Maori have considered the head to be the most sacred part of the body, so they mainly tattoo their faces.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 어법에 맞게 변형하여 쓰시오.

det.korean: tradition(명사) → traditionally(부사): 문장 전체를 수식하는 부사 필요. "전통적으로"
det.analysis:
tradition(명사) → traditional(형용사) → traditionally(부사)
문두에서 문장 전체를 수식하는 부사
Traditionally, S + V = 전통적으로 ~하다
det.tip: tradition → traditional → traditionally — 명사 → 형용사 → 부사

questions.passage: I just knew I had no choice. “All right, Nani,” I replied with a sigh. “I’ll come.” He wanted me to drive him to Murupara to finish his work.
questions.stem: 다음 글에서 할아버지가 와카파파를 완성하기 위해 가고자 했던 장소를 본문에서 1단어로 찾아 쓰시오.

det.korean: "drive him to Murupara to finish his work" → 무루파라
det.analysis:
할아버지의 목적지 = Murupara
"to finish his work" = 와카파파 완성을 위해
det.tip: 고유명사는 대문자로 시작: Murupara

questions.passage: After turning the corner, we saw an old man standing in front of a house. He welcomed Nani Tama with a gentle smile, but in his eyes, I saw the message, “We must hurry.”
questions.stem: 다음 글에서 무루파라의 노인이 할아버지를 반겨준 방식을 본문에서 2단어로 찾아 쓰시오.

det.korean: "He welcomed Nani Tama with a gentle smile" → 온화한 미소
det.analysis:
반겨준 방식 = with a gentle smile
2단어 답 = gentle smile
det.tip: with a gentle smile = 온화한 미소로 — 전치사 with + 방식

questions.passage: For some time, my grandfather had been busy writing down the village genealogy, known as the whakapapa. The whakapapa had been in his old house. But then came the night of the fire, which ran through the house and destroyed our past. In only one night, everything we knew was gone.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?

det.korean: "the fire, which ran through the house and destroyed our past" → 화재로 과거(와카파파)가 소실됨.
det.analysis:
✅ ② 화재로 와카파파 소실: 원문 일치
❌ ① 손주가 운전함, 할아버지 아님
❌ ③ "My boss won’t let me" → 기꺼이가 아님
❌ ④ "shocked to see how thin" → 건강 악화
det.tip: 핵심 사건(화재 → 소실)을 정확히 대조

ch: 할아버지는 혼자 차를 운전해서 무루파라에 갔다.
손주는 기꺼이 휴가를 내고 고향에 갔다.

questions.passage: Now that day seems like a dream to me. I remember the two old men sitting at the table and the soft sounds of the Maori words as they talked. All through the quiet afternoon and into the evening, they recalled missing names. I had a strange feeling that there were other people in the room. I felt as if people from the past were looking over the shoulders of the two old men to see if the work was correct. Finally, they stopped. It was done. After a moment of silence, the old man whispered to Nani, “Goodbye, friend.” Crying, they pressed their noses together to say goodbye.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?

det.korean: 와카파파를 마을에 가져다준 것은 Nani Tama(할아버지)이지, 무루파라의 노인이 아니다.
det.analysis:
❌ ④ 무루파라의 노인이 전달: 원문에서 Nani Tama가 마을에 와카파파를 건넴
✅ ① "All through the quiet afternoon and into the evening" → 일치
✅ ② "a strange feeling that there were other people" → 일치
✅ ③ "pressed their noses together" → 일치
det.tip: 행위의 주체를 정확히 파악: 와카파파를 마을에 건넨 사람 = Nani Tama

ch: 두 노인은 오후부터 저녁까지 빠진 이름을 기억해 냈다.
화자는 과거의 사람들이 방에 있는 것 같은 느낌을 받았다.
작업이 끝난 후 두 노인은 코를 비비며 작별했다.

questions.passage: It was early morning and still dark when we returned to Auntie’s place. All the lights were on, and the village people were waiting for us. Smiling, Nani Tama lifted up the whakapapa and offered it to the village. Our hearts were full because our grandfather had saved our past for us.
questions.stem: 이 글 전체의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 할아버지가 화재로 소실된 와카파파(계보)를 다시 쓰고 완성하는 이야기 → 가문의 역사를 보존하려는 헌신
det.analysis:
✅ ③ 가문의 역사 보존: "saved our past for us" = 과거를 구해냄
❌ ① 요리 문화: 무관
❌ ② 관광 명소: 무관
❌ ④ 문신 기술: Deep Learning 내용이지 본문 주제 아님
det.tip: 글의 주제: "saved our past" = 과거(계보)를 보존하려는 노력

questions.passage: For some time, my grandfather had been busy writing down the village genealogy, known as the whakapapa. The whakapapa had been in his old house.
questions.stem:
다음 진술이 본문의 내용과 일치하면 True, 일치하지 않으면 False를 고르시오.

"The whakapapa is the village genealogy."

det.korean: "the village genealogy, known as the whakapapa" → 와카파파는 마을의 계보이다. → True
det.analysis: ✅ True: "village genealogy, known as the whakapapa" → 정확히 일치
det.tip: "known as" = ~로 알려진 → 와카파파 = 마을 계보

questions.passage: It took Nani Tama almost two years to gather most of the whakapapa, but there were still missing names he needed to fill in. Now, he wanted me to drive him to Murupara to finish his work.
questions.stem:
다음 진술이 본문의 내용과 일치하면 True, 일치하지 않으면 False를 고르시오.

"Nani Tama completed the entire whakapapa by himself within two years."

det.korean: 본문: "almost two years to gather most of the whakapapa, but there were still missing names" → 전체를 완성하지 못했고, 빠진 이름이 있었다. → False
det.analysis: ❌ False: "most"(대부분) ≠ "entire"(전체), "still missing names" → 완성하지 못함
det.tip: most(대부분) ≠ entire/complete(전체) — 부분과 전체의 차이

questions.passage: Tā moko is the traditional Maori art of tattooing, which has been a culturally significant practice of the Maori for thousands of years. It is not only decorative but also symbolic of an individual’s journey from their past to their present. Each curved line and pattern of tā moko represents a person’s whakapapa (genealogy), social positions, and personal accomplishments. This explains why no two tā moko designs look the same.
questions.stem:
다음 진술이 본문의 내용과 일치하면 True, 일치하지 않으면 False를 고르시오.

"All tā moko designs share the same patterns and meanings."

det.korean: 본문: "no two tā moko designs look the same" → 어떤 두 디자인도 같지 않다. "모두 같은 패턴"은 False.
det.analysis: ❌ False: "no two designs look the same" → 모두 다름 ≠ "share the same patterns"
det.tip: "no two X look the same" = 어떤 두 개도 같지 않다 → 모두 고유하다

questions.passage: Smiling, Nani Tama lifted up the whakapapa and offered it to the village. Our hearts were full because our grandfather had saved our past for us. Our Nani Tama smiled again. His smile grew tired. He sighed. “At last, I may go now.” Then, he closed his eyes.
questions.stem:
다음 진술이 본문의 내용과 일치하면 True, 일치하지 않으면 False를 고르시오.

"Nani Tama offered the completed whakapapa to the village before he passed away."

det.korean: "lifted up the whakapapa and offered it to the village" → 와카파파를 마을에 건넨 후, "At last, I may go now"라고 하고 눈을 감았다. → True
det.analysis: ✅ True: 와카파파 전달 → "At last, I may go now" → 눈을 감음 → 시간 순서 일치
det.tip: 사건 순서: 와카파파 전달 → 미소 → 마지막 말 → 눈을 감음
